questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"One of the fiercest debates in the Constituent Assembly centered on the allocation of powers between the Centre and the States. Defending provincial rights, K. Santhanam from Madras warned: 'There is an almost obsessive desire to over-centralize powers in New Delhi. If you burden the Centre with too many administrative responsibilities and starve the provinces of fiscal revenues, the Centre will inevitably break down under its own weight. A financially crippled province cannot maintain schools or hospitals.' In contrast, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Jawaharlal Nehru argued that only a powerful Central government could prevent national disintegration, plan national industrialization, and maintain law and order. The trauma of Partition ultimately decided the debate decisively in favour of a strong, dominant Centre with residuary powers."

Which member from Madras presciently argued in the Assembly that over-centralization would financially cripple the provinces?

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: T.T. Krishnamachari
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.
